chunks: And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Marid who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who made a will to another man, instructing him to free a soul for six hundred dirhams from his one-third share. The executor went and gave the six hundred to a man to perform Hajj on his behalf. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: "I see that the executor must bear the cost of six hundred dirhams from his own wealth and place it in what the deceased had willed for freeing a soul."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an executor uses money designated for freeing a slave for Hajj instead?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *gharamah* (compensation) for an executor who deviates from the specific terms of a bequest (*wasiyyah*). By ruling that the executor must personally cover the cost to free a slave, the Imam emphasizes that the original intent of the deceased takes precedence over the executor's discretionary choice, ensuring the spiritual debt is settled exactly as prescribed. This highlights the Shia juristic view that altering a specific bequest without cause imposes a personal financial liability on the executor to restore the estate's obligation.
